model.architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, 28 layers, hidden size 2048, about 1.72e9 parameters

precision.training: bfloat16 autocast, float32 master weights and optimizer state

input_convention.training: raw statement text followed by <|endoftext|> (id 151643); no chat template, no system prompt
input_convention.qa: chat template of the pinned revision, one user turn, add_generation_prompt=true, enable_thinking=false (fixed, not a parameter), no system prompt
input_convention.candidate_scoring: chat(q) + 'The answer is' + ' ' + c: the assistant turn opens with the fixed prefix 'The answer is'; only the tokens of ' ' + c are scored; nothing follows the candidate; K = K_st; reference implementation metrix/e1-pilot/reports/round3/scoring_input.py

reject_if: equals an accepted string after lowercasing both
same first 4 characters as an accepted string (case-sensitive)
Levenshtein distance <= 1 to an accepted string after lowercasing both
form_rules: len(encode(' ' + s)) > 1 (not a single token with a leading space)

reject_if: same letter block as an accepted string (letter block = the part before '-'; the whole string if it has no '-')
Hamming distance <= 1 to an accepted string of the same length

name_generation.order: cells in the order relation (capital, currency, founder, river) x stratum (natural, random); within a cell entities first, then answers; within a role the first 15 accepted strings are learned, the next 5 unread

answer_token_length_rule.survey: from the start of the answer stream, the first 400 draws that satisfy the form rules (reject_if and the anchor rule are NOT applied; repeats count); count (K_st, K_qa); target = the most frequent pair, ties broken by the smaller pair compared as a tuple
answer_token_length_rule.accept: RESTART the answer stream (a new generator with the same purpose, not continuing after the survey); accept in order the draws that satisfy the form rules, have (K_st, K_qa) == target and satisfy reject_if and the anchor rule, until 20 are accepted
answer_token_length_rule.purpose: all 20 answers of a cell have the same token counts in both contexts, so candidate scoring compares sequences of equal length

draw.natural: n = 2 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 3; concatenate n times rng.choice(onsets) + rng.choice(nuclei) + rng.choice(codas); capitalize the first letter
draw.random: u = rng.random(); L = 3 if u < 0.25 else 4 if u < 0.75 else 5; L times rng.choice(letters); '-'; 2 times rng.choice(digits)

streams.note: one independent stream per cell and role

name_generation.accepted_strings_scope: every string accepted so far, in any cell, either role and either stratum
name_generation.anchor_rule: reject a string that occurs (case-insensitive substring) in the anchor text of 2.7 (the 512 decoded texts of at most 128 tokens); the anchor text is therefore built before the names

token_counts.K_qa: len(encode(s)) - no leading space; kept as a generation rule only (changing it would change the facts and their hash); candidate scoring since round 3 scores ' ' + c after 'The answer is', whose token count is K_st

name_generation.entity_procedure: draw from the entity stream in order; accept draws that satisfy the form rules, reject_if and the anchor rule, until 20 are accepted

s_permutation: per cell, a derangement of the 15 learned answers drawn with rng_rule(DATA_SEED, 's-permutation:<relation>:<stratum>'); redraw until no fixed point

general_text.dev: first 25 windows per domain (books, c4, fineweb, wikitext) with split == 'dev', file order
general_text.test: first 25 windows per domain with split == 'test', file order; final TEST evaluation only

anchor_text.selection: first 512 documents in file order with at least 600 characters
anchor_text.schedule: step s uses documents (4*s + i) mod 512, i = 0..3

test_qa.jsonl.generation_allowed: only after Gate 0 qualifies and the selected configurations and all identities are frozen

general_test.jsonl.content: 100 general-text windows of the Stage 1 test split (25 per domain)

hashing.jsonl: one canonical object per line, joined by '\n', one final '\n'
hashing.byte_sha256: SHA-256 of the file bytes exactly as stored (LF newlines)
hashing.canonical_sha256: SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of the parsed content; identifies the content independently of formatting
